subject: MedNova inference comparison — follow-up & proposed unit-econ tests
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-10-28T16:15:00-07:00
Subject: MedNova call recap + unit-econ test proposal

Quick recap of today's discovery with MedNova (Ellen + procurement Rahul on the call). High-level: they're evaluating Redwood vs HyperscaleX and VendorY for serving a clinical summarization feature. Their asks and constraints: 
- Primary KPI: sub-200ms 95th percentile latency for single-chat queries (avg payload ~350 tokens, final generations avg ~600 tokens).
- Economics focus: want concrete per-1M token comparisons including realistic batching and prefix cache assumptions.
- Security: saw Private offering interest (VPC), but first evals can run on Redwood hosted with an NDA in place.
- Tolerance for quality delta: up to 2% ROUGE reduction if we hit <50% unit-cost delta vs HyperscaleX.

They shared traffic profile (attached CSV) and gave permission for a controlled 1M token run comparing: Redwood hosted (quantized profile), HyperscaleX standard endpoint, and VendorY (their on-prem partner). They specifically want scenarios for: no-cache, 50% prefix-cache hit, 80% prefix-cache hit, and batching at 1, 8, 16 request sizes.

Proposed next steps (feel free to edit):
1) Ben: estimate expected per-1M token cost and 95th p50/p95 latency for the four cache scenarios on our recommended quantization + batching config. Include assumptions (GPU types, concurrency, batch schedules). Target by Thu 10/31 EOD.
2) Laura: draft a short comparison table vs HyperscaleX/VendorY (cost, latency, reliability notes, fallback behavior). Highlight Redwood differentiators (routing, prefix caching, fallback to smaller model). Target by Fri 11/01 AM.
3) I'll reply to Ellen with timeline and ask Rahul for procurement redline expectations + whether they can sign a short SLA for the test.

Attachments: MedNova_traffic_profile.csv (they uploaded) — referenced on the call.

Goals for the test: produce a per-1M token cost matrix + a one-page executive slide that MedNova can take to procurement.

Markus
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-29T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MedNova call recap + unit-econ test proposal

Thanks Markus — good notes. Quick clarifications before I run numbers: 
- For the quantized profile, do we proceed with 8-bit INT quantization + KV-cache enabled (recommended config), or run a FP16 baseline too? My suggestion: primary matrix = INT8 (prod-lean); secondary line item = FP16 for quality check.
- For batching, MedNova's traffic shape indicates a heavy tail (most requests single-user interactive). I'll model two queuing regimes: low-concurrency interactive (target latency) and batched background (nightly bulk).

I'll produce: cost per-1M tokens (tokens generated + prompt tokens), p50/p95 latencies, and compute-hours used. Will call out where automatic prefix caching changes cost vs naive per-token billing. Target: draft numbers by 2028-10-31 18:00 PT.

One quick ask for Laura: if you can pull any public claims HyperscaleX has about per-token pricing or latency SLAs, it helps the comparison narrative.

Ben
Senior Solutions Architect
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@mednova.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@mednova.ai>
Date: 2028-10-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MedNova call recap + unit-econ test proposal

Thanks Markus — appreciate the clear next steps. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 
- We can sign a limited test SLA for the 1M token run; procurement prefers a two-week window for internal review. Rahul, can you confirm estimated speed for redlines?
- Traffic: attached CSV is the production sample over 30 days; median request ~320 tokens, generation avg ~610 tokens. Peak concurrency hits ~120 qps for a short burst (30s) during reports.
- Quality check: our evaluation team can run an automated ROUGE/semantic-similarity sweep if you provide outputs for matched prompts.

Attachments: MedNova_traffic_profile.csv, MedNova_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW draft for initial pilot)

We are happy to schedule the controlled runs next week (Nov 6 — Nov 8 window). If Redwood can provide a one-pager on model fallback behavior (how you tolerate performance vs cost trade-offs) that would be helpful for our architecture team.

Ellen Park
Director, Product
MedNova
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@mednova.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@mednova.ai>
Date: 2028-11-02T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MedNova call recap + unit-econ test proposal

Ellen — thanks, confirmed and appreciate the attachments. Quick reply to confirm alignment and owners: 
- Ben will deliver the unit-econ matrix (INT8 primary, FP16 secondary) and the latency profiles by EOD 10/31 — Ben, please upload draft numbers to the Drive link and ping the HubSpot deal.
- Laura will prepare the competitive summary and a one-pager on fallback model behavior (how we route by cost/latency and maintain graceful degradation). Laura target: 11/01 AM — please include a short suggested canary rollout for the pilot.
- Markus (me): I'll coordinate the test SLA and timeline with Rahul — Rahul, if procurement can push the redline review by 11/03 that gives us time to schedule a run in the Nov 6—8 window.

Immediate asks for the team: 
- Ben: include explicit assumptions on cache hit effects (model the 0%, 50%, 80% prefix-cache hit scenarios) and show effective per-1M token cost under each.
- Laura: capture any public HyperscaleX claims and note where their single-tenant dedicated offering would materially change our economics.

I'll assemble a short exec slide once your artifacts land and share with MedNova. Thanks everyone — Ben/Laura, cc'ed below for visibility.
